title: Add `athena retry <job>` seeded from the introspection record
summary: Add an `athena retry <job>` command that builds the retry request for a rejected or failed job from its introspection record (proposed_request, cause, prevention, earlier cases), plus the original scope and accepted corrections already carried by "try again on". It then reads and shows the reading as `ask` does. The reader's brief shows earlier cases of the same class and any prevention already tried, so a repeat is visible as one. Fixture records in a temp directory verify it.

defaults_applied.how: All new code and tests are Rust.
New tests use fixture records in a temp directory; cargo test and clippy must pass.
One command and its reader-brief wiring, reusing the existing earlier_attempt path.
Behavior is exercised by running the fixture tests and the CLI help.
Details came from design section 3.5, the existing reading.rs retry code and the introspection types.
Doc comments, CHANGELOG entry and messages are written for an outside reader.
The retry starts from the cause record, not the last finding, as C2 in the design requires.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: `athena retry <job>` goes through the same flow as `ask` (reading shown, Enter accepts on a terminal, --yes and --json supported). It never submits a run on its own, per design section 3.5.

The introspection record is read from the job's records through the existing introspection view/record types; the retry request text is the stored proposed_request, with cause, prevention and earlier-case ids added to the EarlierAttempt carried to the reader.
If the job has no introspection record or no proposed_request, the command falls back to today's 'try again on' behavior and says so.
Earlier cases come from the stored earlier_cases ids on the introspection; the retry does not re-run class matching or Jev.
Only rejected or failed jobs can be retried, as with earlier_attempt today.
The design doc's build-order step 2 is left as-is, with at most a short status note.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`: a new test builds fixture records in a temp directory (a rejected job with an introspection record) and shows that retrying it yields a reading input whose request carries the proposed_request, cause and prevention, the original request and the accepted corrections.

Run `cargo test`: a fixture test shows earlier cases of the same class (ids and one-line what) appear in the retry's reader brief, and that a prevention already tried in an earlier introspection of the same class is shown as already tried.

Run `cargo test`: a fixture test shows `retry` on a job that is not rejected or failed is refused with a clear message. A second shows a job with no introspection falls back to the 'try again on' behavior.
Run `cargo run -- retry --help`: the command exists and takes a job argument, with the same --yes and --json options as `ask`.
crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs has a `Retry` subcommand that goes through the same reading display as `ask`, and does not submit the run unless the user accepts.
The reader brief text in athena-context includes the cause, prevention and earlier-case section only when the retry came from an introspection record, with a test of that.
Run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`: all pass with no new warnings.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the new command, and README or CLI docs mention `athena retry <job>` if they list commands.

out_of_scope: Steps 1 and 3 or later of the build order.
Changing introspection generation, class matching or the class registry.
Changes to governance files: athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI, toolchain and lint configuration.
departures: This is a multi-crate change (CLI, core, context) with new fixture tests, so it runs somewhat above the reference cost and time. I read only part of the introspection storage code, which lowers pass odds slightly.
